Unio Employee Benefits Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race, won over this exact course and trip on Good recently; Andrew Slattery's yard is 1/22 over 14 days but Faoladh's recent form line (1 in 6 runs) and Going figures on sim-going are relevant — he is perfectly placed tactically with a clean lead virtually guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh bounced back to winning ways last time out and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, with a our rating of 75 placing him second among the field; the chief concern is a trainer operating at just 5% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Altimara
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Ross O'Sullivan who has winning form over this 7f trip on Good; connections T14 of 1/12 shows modest recent strike rate, but Altimara's sim-going record of 10/15 and two wins from five in similar conditions makes her a legitimate threat off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Altimara has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 72 against an official mark of 68, she holds a clear edge on paper from stall 8; the main concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts, with a fifth the best she has managed recently.

runners_data.name: Naoi
runners_data.note: 402 days off the track is the dominant concern, though the form before the break showed three consecutive top-three finishes including over 7f on Good — W McCreery sends her out fresh with the 5lb claimer Sam Coen, and she handles this going well on the evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for over 400 days, Naoi faces obvious questions on comeback, though three thirds in that sequence show she has placed consistently; she has run over today's trip before, and a rating of 71 offers some encouragement from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Has placed second and won from hold-up in 7f handicaps on Good, and Seamie Heffernan is a major upgrade in the saddle; blinkers/tongue-tie headgear combination noted, and Paul Flynn's runners at 0/24 over 14 days is a negative trainer angle, but the horse's own form over 6-7f is honest.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and showed more with a second three starts back, but an unplaced return last time and a trainer without a winner in 24 recent attempts are real concerns; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 136 lb from stall 20.

runners_data.name: La La Lucrative
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with three wins in similar conditions, currently redistributed into midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with closers; her finish-fade flag and the positional compromise mean her chance is softened in a shape that requires her to break her natural rhythm.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out after winning two starts back, La La Lucrative has experience over today's trip and going in his favour, but an eighth three starts back hints at inconsistency, and 135 lb from stall nine is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: Anthony Oliver's three-year-old is 4/21 for his yard over 14 days which is a solid trainer angle; holds-up and has a fade flag, and the step up from 6f to 7f is a clear question — 0 wins from 7 sim-going runs tempers expectations despite the decent place record.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, All Hail has nonetheless run over today's trip and going before, and a second in recent starts shows some ability; however, back-to-back struggles since make him hard to fancy from stall 7 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran who has hit the frame over 7f on Good before; genuinely wants to be dropped out last, but the crowded field forces him into midfield on the map — his style-fit score of 0.93 reflects the compromise, and a clear run is harder to find in a 21-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and drawn 19 carrying 133 lb, Free Solo faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 71 suggests more ability than his official mark of 63 implies after 48 days off.

runners_data.name: Ballymagreehan
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good for David Marnane and is dropping back in trip; his natural hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield slot by the volume of closers in this race, and the shorter 7f trip combined with a positional disadvantage tempers confidence despite the winning form.
runners_data.comment: Ballymagreehan won four starts back but has posted three modest efforts since, including back-to-back sevenths and a ninth last time out 13 days ago; he has run over today's trip and going before, though his recent consistency is the obvious concern at 132 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: W McCreery saddles this four-year-old who has been prominent in nothing at this trip — all recent runs show double-figure finishes over 6-7f, and the tongue-tie has not unlocked improvement; style-fit concern compounds the modest form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Phoenix Pairc nevertheless steps back up to a trip she has run over before and arrives here fresh on a 17-day break, though she carries 132 lb from stall 12 and her recent sequence of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy her too strongly.

runners_data.name: Mr Perth
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Grassick who has struggled on Good ground, recording a sim-going figure of just 1/4; form over 7-8f has not produced a place at the level, and Wayne Lordan takes the ride without a strong course or going angle to work with here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts with finishes of seventh, unplaced, seventh, and eighth, Mr Perth is hard to fancy at the foot of the weights on 131 lb, and our rating of 65 ranks him 17th of 21 — though he has run over today's trip and returns after a 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this consistent three-year-old who has placed in five of her last six races at 7-8f on Good — Mrs Harrington's yard is 2/31 over 14 days but Bear Right's form profile is genuine; her natural hold-up style is displaced into midfield by the crowd, which may suit if she can track the pace rather than be held up too far back.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless, Bear Right has been placed in her last five starts — second last time out, and thirds two, three, and five starts back — yet she remains yet to win in recent form; drawn in stall three carrying 130 lb, she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's three-year-old won at 6f on Standard and placed at 8f on Good; genuinely wants to sit off the pace but the redistribution means she cannot get her natural position in this field — style-fit at 0.92 is a meaningful discount given that her two wins came at different surface/trip combinations.
runners_data.comment: Kc Bear has run over today's trip and showed a second two starts back, but that eighth last time out is hard to overlook, and 39 days off the track plus 130 lb to carry from stall 17 gives him plenty to contend with.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: The most interesting prominent-style runner behind Faoladh: won over 7f on Good and placed at 8f, with Rory Cleary aboard and Brendan Duke in decent 14-day form at 1/5; second in the betting on these figures would suggest she is expected to track the leader and challenge in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Zheleznaya Dama is hard to fancy at her current level, though a win last time out and just 17 days between runs at least show she is in form and fresh, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Hazrama
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's three-year-old has posted three consecutive last-place efforts from 10th to 19th in field, and the redistribution into midfield compounds a lack of meaningful form; the fade flag is consistent with the form, and this is a tough opportunity for improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Hazrama faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 36-day break plus draw two offer slim crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Shamanka
runners_data.note: Harry Cleary sends this four-year-old out for the first time in 34 days with a tongue-tie; all five recent runs ended outside the money and the sim-going record of 2/10 is uninspiring — forced into midfield despite being a natural hold-up type, improving her chances of involvement seems difficult.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Donohoe who contests prominently and has multiple top-six finishes at 7-8f on Good including a second at 8f; 0/7 for the trainer over 14 days is soft, but Brains is consistent and may benefit from a steady pace if he can sit second or third.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Brains has been consistently held and ranks fifteenth of twenty-one on our figures, making him very hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going and a return after just a fortnight.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's 8-year-old has not won since a 6f run and returns from a 14-day break without strong going form; a genuine closer who is squeezed into midfield on this map, and the 0/5 trainer angle over the same period does not encourage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Gordon Bennett does at least bring experience over today's trip and going, and a third three starts back shows he can get competitive; but a ninth and unplaced effort since then are harder to ignore off 126 lb from stall 21.

runners_data.name: Oppenheimer
runners_data.note: Kevin Coleman's three-year-old is 3/15 for the yard over 14 days which is the main positive; the horse's own form at 6-7f shows finishing 4th-11th consistently without threatening, and forced midfield positioning on this map blunts a naturally held-up style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, Oppenheimer is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround at least suggesting he is fit.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: T G McCourt's four-year-old placed twice from 7 runs at 7f on Good; no jockey listed on the card detail, and the redistribution from a true hold-up slot into midfield means the horse cannot race to its natural rhythm — the 0/11 yard figure over 14 days adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Jazzit is winless in his last six starts, finishing down the field on three of those occasions, and he is ranked last of the 21 runners on our figures, making him very hard to fancy despite a placed effort last time out and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: M D O'Callaghan's three-year-old has only one run at this trip on Good (finishing 6th) and all strong form comes at 5f on Standard; being set up as a hold-up type on a flat 7f track in fast conditions looks an awkward match for the profile.
runners_data.comment: Ninth Crusade shaped with promise when second two starts back, and he has run over today's trip, carrying 139 lb from stall 18; the concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts, and top form has proven elusive.

runners_data.name: Sporting Hero
runners_data.note: William Durkan's six-year-old is a prominent racer who won at 5f on Good and ran 1-6 over recent visits to Good ground; returning after 86 days off is a stamina question over 7f, though the tactical position of racing up with the pace is a genuine fit for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Sporting Hero has won twice in his last six starts, most recently scoring two starts back before a couple of unplaced efforts, and he has experience of today's trip and going; a break of 86 days is the one query, but rated top of this field he remains the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner 7f handicap at Leopardstown and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to pressurise him — he should stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the outset and control the tempo through the middle portion of the race. With Good to Firm ground and a flat straight, he can set a metronomic gallop that neither burns himself out nor invites a cavalry charge from behind. Zheleznaya Dama, Brains and Sporting Hero are the only other truly prominent-leaning types and none is a natural front-runner, so Faoladh's supremacy at the head of affairs looks secure. The redistribution of multiple hold-up horses — La La Lucrative, Kc Bear, Bear Right, Free Solo, Ballymagreehan, Phoenix Pairc, Hazrama, Jazzit, Gordon Bennett, Shamanka and Oppenheimer — into midfield on the map reflects a field that is genuinely overloaded with closers who cannot all find their natural position off the pace; La La Lucrative, Kc Bear and Bear Right are most likely to actually push up towards the prominent slots in a large, competitive field. A controlled, steady-to-modest gallop set by a lone leader strongly favours horses who can race close to the pace and produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs — true hold-up horses must produce a very late surge, which is harder against a soft pace, making the prominent and pace-tracking profiles the tactical sweet spot here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh sets a controlled but honest gallop and none of the prominent types seriously challenge his lead, producing a race where the winner comes from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Faoladh bowls along in front at a measured tempo, and the race develops into a conventional handicap where those racing second or third can pick him off in the final furlong; Good to Firm ground rewards horses racing prominently without the expense of a pace battle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Faoladh Leads Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh's uncontested lead allows him to conserve energy and he quickens or sustains to hold on as the field fails to close in time over 7f.
scenarios.body: With no rival to push him early, Faoladh settles into his own rhythm and the large field behind runs into traffic or fails to produce coordinated late runs, leaving the leader with enough in hand to hold on; his recent course win at this trip on Good ground bolsters this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Finishers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution resolves itself and a cluster of genuine hold-up horses find clear runs in the straight, generating a late-race surge that overtakes a slowing Faoladh.
scenarios.body: The field bunches through the middle stages and the final two furlongs become a sprint finish where those with the highest cruising speed can charge through gaps; horses like Rappell, Altimara and Bear Right, who have placed consistently in similar conditions, are best positioned if the cavalry arrives in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Zheleznaya Dama or Sporting Hero pushes up to track Faoladh closely and the two of them draw clear before the hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: An early two-horse breakaway scenario where pace and natural position prove decisive on fast ground; runners without the speed or position to respond are left stranded as the race becomes a two-length affair at the front.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh's unchallenged lead is the structural key to the race — watch whether any of the prominent types (Zheleznaya Dama, Sporting Hero) push up to press him early, because if they do the dynamic shifts from a controlled pace to a true test.

With 21 runners and a field heavily stacked with redistributed closers, traffic in the straight is a serious risk — horses like Bear Right, Altimara and Rappell need a clear passage from the two-furlong pole or their chances will evaporate regardless of ability.

Sporting Hero is returning after 86 days off the track and stretching from 5f to 7f on fast ground — if he fires early to track Faoladh, watch whether he holds his gallop in the final furlong or ties up, as this would have a direct knock-on for whoever is immediately behind.

runners_data.name: Abbotsford
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo for De Weld who won over 12f on good ground and has strong sim-going credentials (1W1P); wants a prominent position but faces stiff competition for that berth from four rivals and may get shuffled wider than ideal, though Chris Hayes's tactical awareness helps manage that risk.
runners_data.comment: Abbotsford arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, in good heart right now; he carries 133 lb but his recent consistency makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Cannes
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner with a course-and-distance win on good ground to her name; Declan McDonogh can control fractions with no rival to pressure her, and a recent 14th in a strong Curragh handicap should not distract from the quality of her earlier wins — lone speed in a 9-runner field is a powerful asset.
runners_data.comment: Cannes shaped with real promise when third last time out, boasting going experience and a rating of 100 that marks him out as a genuine threat in this field; the worry is that he has managed only one win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Highwayman
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who last won over 12f on good at Leopardstown, but the finish-fade flag is a real concern on fast ground over 1m6f; the 38-day break and unimpressive recent form string (9-0-0-8-1) make him hard to trust, though Scott McCullagh knows O'Brien's horses well.
runners_data.comment: Lowly on our figures and ranked last of the nine runners, Highwayman is hard to fancy despite that recent win, with four defeats around it in his last five starts and a 38-day absence adding to the questions.

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Dual winner at 12-13f on good and soft for Noel Meade, with a terrific recent form string culminating in back-to-back wins; trainer's 0/17 14-day strike rate is a mild flag, but Gary Carroll is enterprising and Madbadanddangerous has the tactical versatility to make a prominent position work.
runners_data.comment: Madbadanddangerous won his last two outings and arrives here in excellent nick after 24 days off, though a career-high 133 lb tests his resolve, and his speed figure of 70 leaves him something to find on our ratings against the principals.

runners_data.name: Piazza San Marco
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR=105 for Aidan O'Brien and Wayne Lordan, but returning from a 298-day absence having last run in a 4-runner heat at the Curragh; the layoff is the dominant question, though the stable fires returners well and his best form on good going is clearly smart.
runners_data.comment: Piazza San Marco landed a win three starts back and shaped with promise when fourth two starts back, suggesting the talent is there — but 298 days off the track is the significant question mark he must answer on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Trojan Fighter
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on good ground for Pat Twomey but has been off 61 days, the longest break in the field, and the tongue-tie is first-time headgear worth noting; his natural hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace genuinely collapses, but the layoff and equipment change introduce uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Trojan Fighter landed a win three starts back and followed up with a fourth two starts back, showing consistent involvement at the business end, and he has run over today's trip before; the main concern is that eighth last time out, combined with 61 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 10-13f on good ground for Harrington and Foley, with the tongue-tie and hood combination suggesting the yard has him tuned up; the prominent style fits this race shape well, and two wins at the distance band in current form makes Wyman one of the most naturally suited horses to how this race should unfold.
runners_data.comment: Wyman arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid claims, though ranked sixth of nine on ratings and carrying 133 lb, he faces a stiff ask against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Keepsgettingbetter
runners_data.note: Steady placer on the all-weather who is a true hold-up horse by nature — pushed into a midfield mapping here because the rear is saturated with closers; Donnacha O'Brien's 2/14 recent strike rate is modest and the OR=79 represents a significant class ask at Listed level, making the style-fit discount meaningful.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Keepsgettingbetter faces a stiff ask here, and her speed rating of 74 leaves plenty to find on the field; she has experience over today's trip and going, and two wins in her last six starts show she knows how to reach the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Teologia
runners_data.note: Three wins from her last three starts over 10-13f on good and soft for Joseph O'Brien and Ben Coen, with the hood suggesting she's at peak sharpness; an excellent sim-going record (2W3P) and a naturally prominent style place her among the most tactically well-positioned runners in this specific race shape.
runners_data.comment: Teologia arrives on the back of three consecutive wins, which is the standout positive, yet our figures rank her seventh of nine in this field, making her hard to fancy at the top level of this contest despite her recent momentum and distance experience.

races.paceDynamic: Cannes is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no natural rival to pressure her, shapes to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m6f at Leopardstown. Behind her, Abbotsford, Madbadanddangerous, Wyman, and Teologia all want prominent positions, creating a genuine scramble for the four or five places directly behind the leader from the outset, with traffic and position battles most likely to ignite two to three furlongs out as the field compresses. Highwayman, Piazza San Marco, and Trojan Fighter are the true hold-up types who will be asked to make ground from behind, though Keepsgettingbetter — a genuine hold-up horse — has been pushed into the midfield map because the rear is already congested; its real position will be further back than shown, and that redistribution tempers its prospects. The field holds more prominent-minded runners than can realistically secure their preferred berth, with Wyman and Teologia — both in excellent recent form and on going they handle — best-placed to actually land the prominent spots behind Cannes; this controlled, moderately-run shape on fast ground ultimately favours progressive, prominent-to-midfield horses who can sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile rather than pure closers who need a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cannes Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Cannes leads at a controlled but honest clip and the prominent runners settle cleanly into position behind her.
scenarios.body: Cannes sets a sustainable pace that suits horses travelling prominently and switching off early, with the prominent group having enough energy to quicken decisively from two furlongs out; Wyman and Teologia, both in superb recent form and adept on good-to-firm, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic battle burns excessive energy through the middle mile and sets up a truly run race despite Cannes's presence.
scenarios.body: Highwayman and Trojan Fighter, genuine hold-up types who last won over this trip on similar going, come with late runs as the prominent group ties up; Piazza San Marco, if bouncing back from a 298-day break with A P O'Brien's renowned freshness angle, could be the wildcard swooping late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Cannes Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that Cannes builds a lead the field cannot claw back in the straight.
scenarios.body: Cannes, who boasts a win over this course and distance on identical going, simply has too much in the tank if rivals waste energy in positional battles and leave it too late; her Joseph O'Brien handler has significant course ammunition and Declan McDonogh is a smart front-rider who can judge the fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses crowd each other into trouble two furlongs out, opening a clear run for a surprising winner.
scenarios.body: Keepsgettingbetter, though racing out of its natural hold-up role and mapped further forward than natural, could benefit if gaps open unexpectedly in a chaotic straight; Madbadanddangerous has the raw form to capitalise if rivals interfere with each other.

watchPoints.text: Abbotsford, Madbadanddangerous, Wyman, and Teologia all want the four prominent positions behind Cannes — watch the first two furlongs for bumping, crossing, and jostling that could unbalance one or more of these closely-rated rivals.

Piazza San Marco returns from 298 days off and, if short of peak fitness, Wayne Lordan may push him forward earlier than natural — monitor his positioning at the break as an unexpected pace-influencer.

Highwayman carries a finish-fade flag on fast ground; if he is asked for an effort from two furlongs out and weakens rapidly, he creates a significant traffic hazard for closers Trojan Fighter and Keepsgettingbetter attempting to come through.

Going is officially Good to Firm at Leopardstown based on all race-day reports — any horse whose sim-going record is thin or negative on fast ground (particularly Keepsgettingbetter's all-weather profile) should be downgraded if the surface plays quick.

Cannes's ability to dictate every fractions unchallenged is the single biggest pace variable in this race — if she is allowed a soft lead through the middle mile, the race shape locks firmly into Scenario A and prominent runners benefit disproportionately.

races.name: Money Back Daily Specials With Tote.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with strong course-and-distance form (1/13f Good, 1/12f Good), gets an uncontested lead on Good to Firm; eight-year-old carries top weight of 142lbs which could blunt finishing effort, but style fit of 0.94 at the head of affairs gives him full tactical control here.
runners_data.comment: Satono Chevalier arrives on the back of three wins in his last six starts, with the most recent coming three starts back, and he handles today's distance and going having tackled both before; the worry is that unplaced run last time out.

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: Lightly-framed four-year-old fitted with a tongue-tie after mixed recent form; three placed efforts at 12-13f on Good suggest a horse that stays this trip adequately, and Shane Foley's booking for a Harrington yard on a 2/31 14-day strike rate is mildly encouraging — drops further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Placed third in two of her last four starts and back quickly after running seventh just eight days ago, Sea Coral has run over today's trip and going and carries a workable 140 lb; yet to win in recent starts, but her rating of 84 marks her as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 108-day break for the same Flannery yard that saddles the favourite; form shows 2nd and 3rd at 16-18f so the extra distance at 1m5f is if anything a slight concern, but a fresh prominent horse may slot just off the leader at a sustainable pace.

runners_data.name: Pavilion End
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose best recent form came over 10-14f on Good ground (2nd, 3rd); Declan McDonogh takes the ride and the 17-day turnaround looks fine, but with this many closers in the field he may struggle to find a clear run until late.
runners_data.comment: Pavilion End has shown consistent placing ability of late, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, though he remains winless in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and returns after 17 days, but 135 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ben Hur
runners_data.note: Strong stayer who has won over 16f on Soft and finished placed twice at that trip on Good; hold-up type who will be ridden patiently by Adam Caffrey, and the step back to 1m5f is borderline though the quicker ground suits — his profile fits a scenario where the pace quickens late and he picks up ground.
runners_data.comment: Ben Hur shaped with clear promise when third last time out, and his speed rating of 82 puts him ahead of his official mark — a gelding who has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 22-day break; the risk is he has been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with three consecutive wins over 12f on Good ground but flagged as a horse who fades in the final stages; the step up to 1m5f on a quicker surface is the key test, and while his OR of 82 is high for this field, the tendency to tie up late tempers confidence significantly.
runners_data.comment: Darius Dark has won three of his last five starts, with a run of three consecutive victories two starts back, but returns from 24 days off ranked eighth of twelve on our rating and carrying 133 lb, and that weight plus the unplaced effort last time give pause.

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse in actuality — his form shows wins from off the pace over 12f — but the crowded field of closers means he is unlikely to get the wide-open rail run he ideally needs; five-year-old has ability on this going but the style-fit tag (0.93) is honest context here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of these on our figures, Celtic Druid faces a stiff ask, and his recent seventh three starts back tempers encouragement from the placed efforts since; he has run over today's trip and going, and back-to-back wins earlier in the sequence at least confirm he can find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Harry's Legacy
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old equipped with a tongue-tie who has finished placed three times at 14-17f on Good; a true hold-up type who is compressed into midfield by the field's pace shape rather than by choice, which materially reduces his chance of getting a clean passage late.
runners_data.comment: Harry's Legacy has been out of the sorts in his last two starts and is winless in his last five, with our rating placing him ninth of twelve — hard to fancy at the weights carrying 130 lb, though a second four starts back and a third five starts back show he can hit the frame, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Four-year-old wearing a plain snaffle (hg:p) who has won over 13f on Good and placed twice; her redistribution to midfield reflects the surplus of hold-up types rather than her natural style, meaning she may race in a less-than-ideal spot — the drop in trip from recent runs is also a slight query.
runners_data.comment: Cooley's Mist ran unplaced last time out and, ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, faces a stiff task here, though he does bring distance and going experience, a win two starts back, and a return after a 20-day break that at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Party Dress
runners_data.note: Six-year-old fitted with a tongue-tie, winning over 15f on Good ground in her history, trained by McCreery who fires on a 2/19 14-day rate; a true closer pushed forward in the map by weight of numbers, but the 28-day break and course form over this trip (5th/15f/Good) give her a platform if she gets daylight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Party Dress nonetheless has experience of today's trip and going, and her rating of 76 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark implies; a step forward on 28 days' rest is plausible, though her recent form makes her hard to fancy outright.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Drills
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old from the Bolger yard who has been consistently mid-pack at 10-12f; steps up to 1m5f for the first time today which is a meaningful unknown, and the form figures of 54795 suggest a horse still finding its level rather than one capable of winning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and beaten a fair way back in each of his last three, Gaelic Drills faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 77 gives him a slender edge over his official mark.

runners_data.name: Lauderdale King
runners_data.note: Four-year-old flagged as a finisher who fades late — a damaging dual warning given the distance — and his hold-up style is displaced to midfield by the crowded field; the 69-day layoff is the longest in the field and trainer-jockey doubling up (Slattery/Slattery) is a curiosity, but the form at 10f suggests this trip is too far.
runners_data.comment: Lauderdale King has managed just a third two starts back amid a largely winless recent spell, and 69 days off the track adds a fitness query; ranked last on our figures and representing a trainer in poor form, he is hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Satono Chevalier is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no identified rival willing or able to press from the outside, should slot comfortably into an uncontested lead at a pace entirely of Seamie Heffernan's choosing over 1m5f on Good to Firm ground at Leopardstown. Gaelic Drills and Ehteyat are the closest things to pace companions from a prominent position, but neither is a natural pace-forcing type and both are likely to settle just off the leader rather than challenge for the front. The field is loaded with genuine hold-up horses — Harry's Legacy, Celtic Druid, Cooley's Mist, Party Dress and Lauderdale King are all true closers who are unlikely to secure their natural rearward position given the sheer volume of similar types, meaning several will race against their instincts in midfield. A soft, regulated gallop set by Satono Chevalier with a cluster of hold-up horses compressed into the mid-pack creates a race shape that strongly favours the lone pace-setter to control the tempo and rewards any horse capable of tracking the leader from a prominent position and sustaining the effort into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chevalier Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Chevalier is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested pace throughout with no horse willing to close him down early.
scenarios.body: Heffernan controls the fractions from the front, the field strings out behind, and the race becomes a test of who can best handle a steady-then-quicken shape in the straight; hold-up horses lose ground as the pace lifts and the leader's stamina-based advantage over this longer trip proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Tracks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent or early-mid-pack types tracks Chevalier closely throughout and outstays him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The race is run at a pace that suits those close to the leader, and a horse with better finishing resolution than Chevalier — particularly over 1m5f on quicker ground — sweeps past in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Field Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the middle stages to stretch the field and create a true test of stamina that brings hold-up horses into play.
scenarios.body: A closer with genuine finishing kick — ideally one whose redistribution to midfield in the map reflects real displacement rather than style misfit — manages to thread through and run on when the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Wide-Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Chevalier either misses the break or weakens sharply having set a contested pace, causing the race shape to fragment entirely in the final quarter mile.
scenarios.body: Without the lone pace anchor, the field bunches and the result depends on momentary luck in running and tactical awareness; lower-rated closers with course form get a rare opportunity.

watchPoints.text: Satono Chevalier is the sole pace-setter and if Heffernan is allowed to regulate fractions entirely unchallenged, even an eight-year-old carrying 142lbs has a material chance of controlling this race from pillar to post — watch whether anything from Ehteyat or Gaelic Drills attempts to press him into the second quarter mile.

The field contains at least five genuine hold-up horses (Harry's Legacy, Celtic Druid, Cooley's Mist, Party Dress, Lauderdale King) who are all likely to be racing against their natural instincts in midfield — watch for traffic problems and choking in the straight when the pace lifts.

Darius Dark has produced three consecutive wins but is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, and his first attempt at 1m5f on faster ground than his wins came on is the pivotal unknown — watch whether Ben Coen commits him earlier than ideal to compensate.

Ben Hur's profile — two placings over 16f on Good and a win at that trip on Soft — makes him one of the most interesting hold-up types if the pace produces a genuine stamina test in the final two furlongs; watch whether Caffrey positions him closer than his usual rearward berth.

Pavilion End has placed twice at 14f on Good for O'Brien with McDonogh now taking over; watch for him to be produced with a wide run in the straight as the more patiently-ridden horses get compressed — his shorter-trip speed (3rd/10f/Good) could be a late advantage.

races.name: Dublin To Bahrain Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator who needs to come from well off the pace; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is useful on a light weight, but with this field stacking hold-up horses into midfield, finding clear daylight late on a flat track will be the real test.
runners_data.comment: Pink Oxalis arrives here 21 days on from her latest outing in solid nick, and has run over today's trip and conditions before; a second two starts back gives her claims, and a rating of 96 makes her the one to beat, though she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners a horse who has placed well on good ground but has slipped to OR 85 after a run of near-misses; tongue-strap worn, comfortable waiting style, though getting outpaced through the middle stages on fast ground is a recurring pattern in the form string.
runners_data.comment: Mallavelly has been placed twice in her last three, third two starts back and runner-up three starts back, and she returns on a quick turnaround having run over today's trip and going; the risk is that a sixth last time out raises questions about consistency.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Scott McCullagh rides a filly who showed sharp improvement when winning at 7f on good recently then chased home a winner at 6f; this step back to a flat mile on similar ground suits, and she should slot in just off Thrifty Of Digby, a prime spot in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and placed three starts back, Glory To Be arrives here with experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 89 marks her as a lively threat; the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Duchess Of Kenli
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and rapidly progressive three-year-old who won on good ground at 8f on most recent start; Joseph O'Brien's operation in form, Declan McDonogh retains the ride, and her natural prominent style places her beautifully in the slipstream of the lone front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and her speed rating gives little encouragement, though she does bring a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with 26 days between runs suggesting she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Thrifty Of Digby
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won twice on good ground at this trip and longer; Shane Foley can roll along uncontested here, and while he was pulled up on heavy ground recently, the return to Good To Firm removes that concern — the question is whether he has enough acceleration if rivals collar him late.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is encouraging, but a pull-up two starts back is a concern; Thrifty Of Digby has run over today's trip and her two wins in her last six starts show she can find the line, though 131 lb makes life harder from stall four.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Five-day turnaround for K J Condon's filly who has won on good ground at 10-12f; her natural racing style is to come from well off the pace over longer distances, and being pushed into a midfield role on a shorter, faster trip works against her instincts and her proven distance range.
runners_data.comment: Marmeladova showed she retains ability with a win three starts back, but sixth last time out and a quick five-day turnaround give pause; she has run over today's trip and going, and 128 lb from stall seven keeps her squarely in the midfield mix.

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides a horse whose recent form is excellent — two wins from the last three runs on good ground at 8-9f; however, her natural hold-up style is compromised by the race shape, and she will need to race a position or two further forward than she would prefer to remain competitive.
runners_data.comment: Bella Colombia sits at the foot of our rankings in a field of eight, and while she carries 125 lb from stall 5 and has run over today's distance and going before, it is hard to look past a rating well below most of her rivals despite back-to-back wins in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners a horse wearing a tongue-strap who has shown modest form at this distance and was well beaten on his last two starts at 8-9f on good ground; trainer Weld is patient with his horses but the OR of 72 and recent consistency issues make him a tough sell here.
runners_data.comment: Tachos shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and her experience over today's trip and going counts in her favour from stall one carrying 122 lb; the risk is that she remains winless in her last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Thrifty Of Digby is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Shane Foley can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good To Firm ground over this flat Leopardstown mile without ever being pressured into burning fuel. Glory To Be and Duchess Of Kenli are the natural prominent horses who will track Thrifty Of Digby through the early and middle stages, creating a compact, well-organised front group and ensuring the pace does not collapse. Marmeladova and Bella Colombia are true hold-up horses who cannot get to their preferred position in this shape and have been mapped to midfield, meaning the back of the field will be thinly populated and the closing kick from deep is a weakened threat. This race shape — a lone front-runner controlling a honest but uncontested tempo — heavily favours prominent raiders who can travel in the slipstream and produce a clean turn-of-foot over the final two furlongs without having to make up excessive ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thrifty Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Thrifty Of Digby bowls along uncontested and the pace is fair but not suicidal, the prominent hangers-on strike hardest.
scenarios.body: Thrifty Of Digby sets a rhythm that allows Glory To Be and Duchess Of Kenli to travel smoothly in his wake before unleashing finishing kicks that the hold-up horses, forced to race too far forward, cannot match from midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even slower than expected and Thrifty Of Digby's rivals fail to accelerate sharply enough to reel him in over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With a soft gallop cementing his advantage and a flat track removing any stamina test, Thrifty Of Digby conserves energy through the race and simply outstays pursuers who lack the speed to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves a fraction stronger than anticipated and the prominent horses over-commit, leaving those mapped to midfield with a clear run late.
scenarios.body: Bella Colombia and Marmeladova, both in better form than their OR suggests, find daylight and rattle home, benefiting from a pace that finally suits their closing style even from a compromised position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong and the front group ties up badly entering the final furlong, releasing a late charge from deep.
scenarios.body: Pink Oxalis or Mallavelly, both genuine hold-up operators, swoop from the rear and catch rivals who have emptied, though the redistribution of true closers to midfield makes this scenario dependent on an unlikely collapse at the front.

watchPoints.text: Duchess Of Kenli is lightly raced and rapidly progressive — if she travels with the easy confidence her last win suggested, Declan McDonogh will have her perfectly placed behind Thrifty Of Digby and she could hit the front before rivals realise.

Bella Colombia and Marmeladova are both genuine hold-up horses racing out of their natural position in midfield; watch whether Ben Coen or Donagh O'Connor attempt to drop them out fully anyway, which would increase their ground-loss risk on this flat, fair track.

Glory To Be's trainer M C Grassick is in a small but sharp vein of form (T14: 1/3) — watch the market for any late support that signals stable confidence ahead of a race shape that suits her prominent style.

The going reports confirm Good To Firm for this 8:00 race and have been consistent all evening — no late softening expected; horses with CONCERN flags on fast ground are not present here, but the premium on speed and a clean early position is reinforced by the surface.

Thrifty Of Digby's recent form includes a pulled-up run over 10f on soft, which is irrelevant to tonight — watch whether he is allowed to stride on early or if Foley settles him, as the tempo he sets will determine whether this is a clean front-runner's race or a sprint finish for the prominent pair.
